statements: Decree No. 554/GOV supplies a newer Lao official legal-control source relevant to DPRK IT-worker revenue because it covers UNSC Resolution 1718 designations and requires ongoing screening, immediate withholding/freezing and reporting, list circulation, and false-positive verification. The decree does not identify an IT worker, facilitator, company or enforcement action.
Reporting entities must screen transactions, services and customers against proliferation-financing designations on an ongoing basis.
Suspected designated-person activity must be reported and relevant funds withheld or frozen without prior notice under the decree's procedures.
Potential name matches must be verified and false positives released, supporting a multi-identifier approach rather than name-only adverse action.
UNSC list updates are to be circulated and published through official channels.
Decree No. 554/GOV was dated September 4, 2025 and states an effective date of November 4, 2025.
limitations: General law and administrative framework effective November 4, 2025; not a designation, investigation, charge, asset-freeze result, conviction, or proof of implementation against a catalog subject.

Existing work captures the 2023 APG shortcomings and historic Laos operating-hub evidence. This later decree is a distinct official legal development, but no public IT-worker-specific enforcement result was found.
Do not imply that the decree proves effective enforcement or a completed freeze.
Do not claim an IT-worker case unless a separate official source identifies one.
Use multiple identifiers and escalation because Article 14 expressly addresses false-positive name matches.
Do not retain identity-document numbers or financial selectors.
The reviewed PDF is an AMLIO-hosted unofficial English translation; September 4, 2025 is the decree date, not a separately verified web-publication date.

sources.support: Decree No. 554/GOV supplies a newer Lao official legal-control source relevant to DPRK IT-worker revenue because it covers UNSC Resolution 1718 designations and requires ongoing screening, immediate withholding/freezing and reporting, list circulation, and false-positive verification. The decree does not identify an IT worker, facilitator, company or enforcement action. Exact source support: The decree applies targeted financial-sanctions controls to UNSC designations including Resolution 1718. It requires ongoing customer due diligence; immediate withholding, suspension or freezing and reporting to MOPS and AMLIO; publication and circulation of list updates; reporting of suspected designated-person activity; and verification of possible false-positive name matches. Article 37 states an entry-into-force date of November 4, 2025. Translation note: The PDF labels itself an unofficial translation. Its face states Decree No. 554/Gov., dated September 4, 2025; that is the instrument date, not a separately verified web-publication date. The directly accessible AMLIO-hosted PDF replaces a Bank decree-index file URL that returned an HTML error page during the August 12, 2026 recovery check
